One-bit pixel art background for a 2D adventure game on a handheld console with a black-and-white screen: strictly two colours, black and warm white, no greys at all, no colour. The native screen is 400 pixels wide: the whole picture is built from crisp square art pixels of one size on one regular grid (each art pixel a square block of about 3 by 3 image pixels), as if the small screen were enlarged without smoothing; no anti-aliasing, no blur, no mixed pixel sizes, no soft edges. Grey tones and light exist only as ordered dither patterns of single art pixels: a checkerboard for 50 %, regular dot grids for 25 % and 12 %, and horizontal line patterns for the sky and the sea; shading changes by switching between these patterns with clean borders. Clear silhouettes with one-pixel black outlines, large readable shapes, hand-placed pixel clusters for stones, slates and planks, like a carefully pixelled screen of an early black-and-white home computer game.

Lighting at dusk, high contrast: the upper sky is solid black with a few single-pixel white stars and becomes lighter towards the horizon through bands of horizontal line patterns, up to a band of white light along the horizon; a few long low clouds. The sea is drawn with horizontal dashes, lighter near the horizon. The cottage window and the lantern glass are solid white; the lighthouse lamp is only a small white spot without any beam, rays or glow; no smoke from the chimney (the light beam, the light halos and the smoke are animated separately in the game). Dark objects stand against light ones and light objects against dark ones; the stone slabs of the quay surface are light so that a dark character walking on them reads clearly.

Side view with a fixed camera at standing eye level, like one screen of a 2D adventure game. The harbour-master's cottage stands on the left edge (partly cut off by the left image border), its door about one third of the image height. Wide landscape composition; keep all important things inside the middle 90% of the image height. The horizon lies at about 42% of the image height. The flat walkable top surface of the quay (large stone slabs) is a wide horizontal band from about 60% to 72% of the image height across the whole width, seen slightly from above; below it the front face of the quay wall with large stone blocks down to dark water at the bottom edge, kept simple (a dialogue box will cover it). The iron lantern on its wooden post stands on the quay a little to the right of the cottage; the two barrels, the stack of crates and the coil of rope stand along the back edge of the quay; the middle part of the quay surface stays free for the characters to walk. The short wooden jetty leads from the back edge of the quay into the water in the middle of the picture, the two small fishing boats are moored beside it. On the right, a little further away, the rocky headland with the white lighthouse, its one band drawn black, its top at about 12% of the image height. Few big objects, friendly, slightly stylised shapes. Not a photograph, not a 3D render, not a painting, not a greyscale picture.

Location: the small harbour of Lornholm, a fictional island in a northern sea, at dusk. A stone quay with a short wooden jetty runs along the lower third of the picture. Two small wooden fishing boats are moored at the jetty. On a rocky headland on the right stands a white lighthouse with one red band, its lamp lit. On the left a small stone harbour-master's cottage with a lit window and a smoking chimney. On the quay: two barrels, a stack of crates, a coil of rope and an iron lantern on a wooden post. Calm sea, low clouds, a band of orange light at the horizon, the first stars.

Leave the quay in the foreground free of characters: it is a game background, characters are added later as separate sprites.

No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

One-bit pixel art character sprite sheet for a 2D adventure game on a handheld console with a black-and-white screen: strictly two colours, black and white, no greys, no colour. The first reference image is a pose sheet rendered from a 3D model: copy its layout exactly, with the same 8 walking frames in the top row and the same 4 standing frames in the bottom row, at the same positions and the same scale, with the same body pose and the same leg positions in every frame. The second reference shows the costume and the proportions of the character: take only the costume and the proportions from it; drawing style, resolution and colours follow this description. Each figure is about 56 art pixels tall, every art pixel a crisp square block of the same size on one regular grid (about 4 by 4 image pixels), as if a small game sprite were enlarged without smoothing; no anti-aliasing, no blur, no soft edges, no grey. Tones exist only as black areas, white areas and ordered dither patterns of single art pixels: black fur on the body, legs, arms and ears; the broad white stripe from the nose over the forehead, white cheeks and white muzzle, the black stripe through the eye with a one-pixel white highlight in the eye, a black nose tip at the end of the pointed snout, a small smile; the cap solid black with a one-pixel white edge along the peak and a white button; the vest in a 50 % checkerboard dither with a black outline; white shirt sleeves; the knitted scarf in bold black and white horizontal stripes; the parcel white with a black string cross; the satchel in a dot-grid pattern. A one-pixel black outline around the whole figure; the figure stays readable as a silhouette. Side view facing right.

Layout: Top row: 8 frames of a smooth walk cycle walking to the right that follow the leg positions of the pose sheet (left heel touches down, weight down, legs passing, up, right heel touches down, weight down, legs passing, up); the body bobs slightly, the free arm swings opposite to the legs, the back end of the scarf flutters behind, the parcel stays under the near arm in every frame. Bottom row: 4 frames standing still facing right with the feet as in the pose sheet: 1 standing relaxed, mouth closed, eye open; 2 the same pose with the eye closed (blink); 3 talking, mouth open, the free paw raised in a small gesture; 4 talking, mouth half open, the paw lower. All 12 figures at exactly the same scale, evenly spaced with clear empty space between them, the feet of each row on one baseline.

The badger courier: an original mascot character, a stout, short-legged badger with a broad black-and-white striped face, wearing a dark green peaked cap with a brass button, a dark green vest with pockets over a cream shirt with rolled-up sleeves, a long red knitted scarf, a brown leather satchel on a shoulder strap, and a brown paper parcel tied with string under one arm.

Isolated on a fully transparent background, no ground, no shadows, no glow, no frame borders, no grid lines. No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.
